b: Definition. A superficial linear tear in the squamous lining of the anal canal below the dentate line , usually caused by passing a hard stool.
The commonest cause of painful bright red rectal bleeding at any age, and common in infancy.

% are in the posterior midline (poor blood supply there). A fissure off the midline should make you think of other causes: Crohn's disease, tuberculosis, syphilis, herpes, HIV, anal cancer, leukaemia or lymphoma, or in children, sexual abus

The vicious cycle: hard stool tears the anoderm, pain causes spasm of the internal sphincter , spasm reduces blood flow and prevents healing, so the fissure persists and constipation worsens because the person fears defecation.
Raised resting anal pressure from internal sphincter hypertonia is found in most patients.
